item.speaker: summary
item.prompt: The Summary's version of why deep plain networks degrade and how residual learning fixes it. One claim overclaims - find the passage that limits it.

statements.text: On CIFAR-10, the 56-layer plain network has higher training error (and test error) than the 20-layer plain network.
statements.why: Figure 1, as described in the paper, reports exactly this.

sourceRefs.quote: The deeper network has higher training error, and thus test error.

statements.text: This degradation in deep plain networks is not caused by overfitting.
statements.why: The paper states this directly as an unexpected finding.

sourceRefs.quote: such degradation is not caused by overfitting

statements.text: Residual learning reformulates the problem so stacked layers fit F(x) := H(x) − x instead of the desired mapping H(x) directly.
statements.why: This is the paper's explicit reformulation of the building block.

sourceRefs.quote: we let the stacked nonlinear layers fit another mapping of F(x) := H(x)−x.

statements.text: Residual learning works because identity mappings are always the optimal mapping for every layer.
statements.why: The paper explicitly says identity mappings are unlikely to be optimal in real cases; the reformulation only helps precondition the problem, it doesn't assume identity is optimal everywhere.

sourceRefs.quote: In real cases, it is unlikely that identity mappings are op- timal, but our reformulation may help to precondition the problem.

hints: Which statement claims something is 'always' true, when the paper calls it 'unlikely' in real cases?

outro.speaker: mira
outro.text: Case closed on the degradation mystery: it's an optimization problem, not overfitting, and residual learning just makes identity easier to approach - not guaranteed optimal.
